newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama won't rehire fired air traffic controllers.
newsitem.headline: Panama won't rehire fired air traffic controllers.

text.p: Panamanian air traffic controllers fired last week after a crippling strike will not be re-hired, a Civil Air Service spokeswoman said on Wednesday.

"Our position has not changed," the spokeswoman said, rejecting an olive branch extended by the fired 88 of 94 air traffic controllers who said they were willing to return to work after being dismissed.

The spokeswoman said the government will continue with its plan to use four traffic controllers from the United States to work during peak international traffic hours at Panama's Tocumen International Airport. The replacement workers will also train new controllers.
Traffic at Tocumen, currently operating at 80 percent, is not scheduled to return to normal until the middle of next year.
The air traffic controllers were demanding a pay hike to $2,000 a month from an average of $600 and a special retirement package allowing them to retire earlier than the national average.
